lead: every other person you took somewhere is on the far side of a door you did not go through. she is at the kitchen table, and what put her there was a thing you said out loud, on purpose.
sun: the route was a whole year long and it worked, from the arrivals hall to the afternoon she signed a lease in her own name. she has been on the other side of that since she was twenty-four, and every move you have for a person got spent in the twelve months before it. the turning-round place, in this one instance, is a kitchen you eat in every night.
moon: The Crown does not issue endings. what was said that afternoon was undertaken level, on purpose, by two people who could each have declined, and nothing in it terminates. so the standing-still that normally lasts an afternoon on a platform has been going on for nineteen years, indoors, with the person you delivered sitting across from it and no instruction anywhere for what you do next.
pull: one person in your life arrived and you did not turn round. nineteen years of standing at that edge, in a house, under an undertaking that leaves you nowhere else to be.
tension: her family tell it as a rescue and so do yours, and inside the house you both know it was a route with a wedding at the end, which is the better story and cannot be told. what has no telling is the flatness that came down the week she stopped needing directions. her name has never been in it and it has never lifted, and every sentence available for it sounds like somebody regretting a promise.
cost: she was reading her own post inside a year and working by the spring, faster than almost anybody does it, because somebody went ahead of her at every turn of it. that year was the whole supply. she has been over there ever since, and the one who took her has had nothing to do in this house for nineteen years.

lead: your name went on the call-out list at nineteen and the two above it are dead, so whether a search goes on now gets asked and answered inside the same person, on the slope.
sun: nothing about the work has changed since you were nineteen — you go up, you find them, you bring them down at whatever rate the injured one can manage, and it ends at the open doors of an ambulance with the night going on inside without you. hundreds of those. nothing in that has ever asked whether you were senior, and the descent is still the only part of the job you are good at.
moon: seniority landed before you had a use for it, and what The Heart does to a rescue is make everything terminate in you. the young ones bring a decision up the slope and it stops, because there is nobody on the next rung. so a life spent taking people to a boundary and turning round at it has made you the boundary.
pull: every road you know ends at a boundary you turn round at. the list has made you one, and nothing above your name on it is alive to take a decision off you.
tension: after a bad one the room turns to you, and what it reads is somebody who has made a peace with the thing, and the word they use is steady. it is a blank — the same blank you have stood in at the end of the good nights too, and it has never turned into anything that could be handed on. nobody is placed to check it, because nobody is above you to check anything.
cost: twice a winter somebody comes off that ground alive who would not have, and the reason is one person knowing the ground and not hurrying them. the position added a second job with no route in it. they come to you now to have a thing settled, and settling is not a walk. the ground has nothing to say about that and neither has the list.

lead: he had not been inside a school since the spring. his reason, his mother's reason and the school's reason were all true, and the thing holding him was underneath all three and had been there since he was six.
sun: you cannot lay a route on a person until you know what they are standing on. the eight months began underground, in the year his household came apart. what went on top of that was small and ordinary: two mornings a week, a phased return, a walk to the gate at ten. he sat his exams. he is in another city now and puts it down to having got his head straight.
moon: what goes down does not come up when the route ends. he arrived, walked on, and the dig was left open where it had got to that week, two layers short, with the one person able to confirm it now unreachable and fine. you are still on it. no use exists for the answer, and that has never slowed anything.
pull: he got where he was going in eight months. the reason he could not go, which took you two years and is still not at the bottom, belongs to nobody now.
tension: a household that came about a school place gets asked about the winter the grandmother moved in, and half of them decide, correctly, that this is more than they asked for. two took the boy elsewhere in the second week, to somebody who did the mornings and nothing else, and that held for a term. the ones who let you go down get the eight months, and a person who will not leave anything where it was handed over.
cost: the ones patched at the surface are back inside a year and he has not come back — the difference is a stranger who got under the household before touching the timetable. nine of these have had the bottom of themselves reached by you, and the reaching finished after each family had gone. nobody is left to be told what was under that boy.

lead: the crowd goes down the closed road as one animal, and everyone in it comes away with the same day. yours came apart into six errands out of the side of it, and the day is missing from you.
sun: each of those was a delivery: the woman who had to get to the station, the boy whose lot had gone on without him. you take them out through the side, get them to the place, hand them over and turn back — and the road has moved half a mile on by then, so you re-enter a stretch of it you have never seen, among people you have not been walking with.
moon: for the first half hour it carries you, the only time in your life the moving is not yours to supply, and you would have stayed in it. then somebody two rows over goes down. by the end you have been in and out of that crowd six times; the count is taken at the start and the finish, and you were at a taxi rank for both.
pull: the animal has one day and it keeps it. what you have is six people delivered off the side of it, and no memory of the thing they will all be talking about.
tension: by the following weekend everybody has the same day, the rain and the singing on the way home, and nothing about it changes after that. yours is a taxi rank, a first-aid post, and a chemist. when it comes up you nod along to a thing you were not present for, and the people who say you would not know, you were off somewhere, are being accurate about you in a way they think is a joke.
cost: in a body that size the person coming apart in the middle gets somebody who knows the side streets and is not carried past them. the thing the crowd exists to make — one day, held by everybody at once — happens every year in a place you keep leaving. you have gone since you were twenty-two and have no share in the only part of it that lasts.
